bites.title: Virtual environments
bites.body: A virtual environment gives a project its own set of installed libraries. python -m venv .venv creates one with the standard library. uv venv does the same job with the uv tool, which is also fast at installing packages. Activate the environment before you install or run, so you are not changing the Python that belongs to the whole computer. Two projects can then use two versions of the same library.
bites.sourceNote: Python venv docs and the uv documentation · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why give a project a virtual environment?

choices.text: So its libraries stay separate from other projects

questions.explanation: Each environment has its own installed packages. Projects stop stepping on each other's versions.

questions.prompt: Which command uses only the Python standard library to create an environment?
questions.explanation: venv is included with Python. uv is a separate, faster tool that can also create environments.

bites.title: Dependency files
bites.body: requirements.txt is a list of packages, often with versions pinned, like requests==2.32.3. pyproject.toml is the modern project file and can list dependencies too. A pin makes next month's install match today's. An unpinned name installs whatever is newest, which may break the code. Commit the dependency file. Do not commit the virtual environment folder itself.
bites.sourceNote: Python packaging user guide · confidence: high

questions.prompt: What does requests==2.32.3 in a requirements file mean?
questions.explanation: The == pin asks the installer for that version, so the environment is repeatable.

questions.prompt: What should you commit to Git?

choices.text: The dependency file, not the environment folder

questions.explanation: The dependency file lets someone rebuild the environment. The environment folder is local and large.

bites.title: Version control with Git and GitHub
bites.body: Git stores snapshots of your project, called commits. A branch is a line of commits you can use to try a change without losing the main line. GitHub is a website that hosts Git repositories. It is not Git itself. Before you ask an assistant for a big edit, commit or at least look at git status, so you can see the diff and return to a known snapshot.
bites.sourceNote: Git basics and GitHub docs · confidence: high

questions.explanation: A commit records the project at one moment so you can compare and return to it.

questions.prompt: How are Git and GitHub related?

choices.text: Git is the version-control tool; GitHub hosts Git repositories
GitHub replaces the need to commit

questions.explanation: You can use Git locally with no GitHub. GitHub is one place to store and share a repository.
